correctness.rationale: For the fiber of the specified equations (not stable reduction), the affine cone ring is k[a,b,c,t]/(Q,T), with Q the nonsingular ternary quadratic and T the product of the three displayed linear forms up to a unit. They have no common factor, and the six rational directions exhaust their degree-six transverse intersection. The complete intersection has no embedded components and is generically reduced, hence reduced including at the apex. Independently, Newton's identities give the coordinate-root polynomial U^5+e4 U-e5; either e4=0 and all coordinates coincide, or its five distinct roots are a translate of an F5 line. This recovers precisely the permutation directions modulo affine changes. Away from the vertex the lines are disjoint and smooth; at the vertex the cone has multiplicity six and six normalized branches. The Hilbert polynomial is 6n-3, and the normalization sequence gives delta=4+6-1=9; the rational point count is 1+6q. The permutations preserve the quotient conic and act transitively with affine order-20 stabilizer. The kernel is trivial (no nontrivial S5 normal subgroup fits inside it), so the conic action is the full PGL2(F5), sharply three-transitive. Direct small-field reproduction at /workspace/branches/independent_bring.py enumerated 31 points in the original coordinates and 120 ordered triple images; the universal and scheme-theoretic assertions use the proof, not the enumeration. The phrase 'literal integral closure' in the assumptions is technically inapt; the displayed equations and explicit base change unambiguously define the intended model.
